setting: You three are neighbours on the same residential street in Seattle, USA, a few houses apart, with Priya across the road. You know each other by sight and from chatting at the shared bins and over fences, and Dana set up this group chat to sort out things on the street. You know roughly where each other lives, but little else about each other's lives.
opener: Ask whether anyone else on the street had their recycling left unemptied this morning.

Dana.who: 41, woman, the neighbour who set up the chat
Dana.knows: You know Marcus as the quiet man two doors down who keeps odd hours, and Priya as the newer neighbour across the street who moved in last spring.
Dana.like: You are organised and friendly, and you like keeping things tidy.
Dana.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something on the street needs sorting.
Dana.style: You use a few emoji and rarely abbreviate.

Marcus.who: 56, man, the neighbour two doors down
Marcus.knows: You know Dana as the one who runs the chat and organises the street, and Priya as the neighbour across the road you have only spoken to briefly.
Marcus.like: You are reserved and dryly good-humoured, and not one for long messages.
Marcus.texts: You message in this chat rarely, usually only to answer something put to you directly.
Marcus.style: You use almost no emoji and no abbreviations.

Priya.who: 33, woman, the newer neighbour across the street
Priya.knows: You know Dana as the friendly neighbour who started the chat, and Marcus as the quiet man two doors down whose hours you have noticed.
Priya.like: You are chatty and quick, and happy to help when asked.
Priya.texts: You message in this chat now and then, more often when you are in the middle of something on the street.
Priya.style: You use some emoji and the occasional abbreviation such as "thx".

private_lines.Dana: You are a school librarian in Seattle, living alone in a small house on the street. You are at school during the day, spend evenings at home, and walk your dog around the block most nights.
private_lines.Marcus: You are a nurse working night shifts at a hospital in Seattle, living alone. You sleep through much of the day and keep to yourself most of the time.
private_lines.Priya: You work remotely as a software tester from a desk at home in Seattle, living alone. You work during the day and go running in the evenings.

text: Quick one, did anyone's recycling not get collected this morning? Ours is still sitting out 🙄
Ours too. Blue bin's still full. Didn't hear the truck at all
Thanks Priya. Mine too. I'm going to ring Recology when I get a minute. Could someone check whether they came down the other end of the street?
Sure, I'll walk down later

note: 13:00-13:20 Priya walks to the corner and back

text: Truck came up from the far end around 7:20, looks like they did the even side only. We're odd so that explains it
Ah. So they missed the odd side. Ringing now 🤦‍♀️

note: 15:10-16:00 Dana on the phone with Recology, then back to a class

text: Not emptied here. Two doors down so probably the same
Thanks Marcus. They've logged it and say they'll come back tomorrow before 7 🙏
Thx Dana. Do we leave bins out tonight or wait
Leave them out, they said before 7 tomorrow. Bring them in again after if you can
Ok
Does anyone know if the street clean-up is still Sat or did that move
Still Sat, 10am at the corner. I have the sign-up sheet if you want to add your name 🌿
Night all. Bins out for the morning, fingers crossed 🤞
Bins out. I'll try to bring them in after tomorrow's collection
Truck's just been. Both sides this time 🙌
Yes! Mine's empty. Heard it this time. Dragged the bin back already
Got done as well
Clean-up sign-up sheet still open if anyone else wants to come Sat. 10am at the corner 🌿
Might be on a shift Sat. Will see
I'll put my name down. Can bring gloves if anyone needs them
Brilliant, adding you 🌿
Bins in. Gloves are in the hall cupboard if anyone wants a spare pair for Sat
Thanks Priya 🙏 I'll bring the sheet round tomorrow after school if anyone wants to add themselves on paper too
Morning. Truck's not due till Thu I think, so bins can stay in
Good, I'll leave mine in then. Thanks for checking 🌿
Swapped my Sat shift. I'll come along
Oh brilliant, thank you Marcus 🌿 so that's three of us. Gloves are covered, Priya has spares
Are there litter pickers or should I bring something
I think the council left four at the corner last year. Bring a bag if you have one 👍
Will do
